reason: H0 fuzzes PNG decoding only after installing a buffer or stream. It never exercises the metadata-setting protocol represented by SPNG_SET_CHUNK_BOILERPLATE, including encode-only operation and interactions between user-supplied metadata and same-type chunks in the PNG. Those states materially alter S1 behavior: read_non_idat_chunks conditionally discards or preserves file data based on ctx->user.exif, ctx->user.text, ctx->user.splt, and ctx->user.time.
evidence: H0 always calls spng_set_png_stream() or spng_set_png_buffer() before its chunk getters and never invokes a metadata spng_set_* operation.
SPNG_SET_CHUNK_BOILERPLATE sets ctx->encode_only when ctx->data == NULL, a state H0 cannot enter because it installs PNG input first.

S1 contains user/file conflict branches such as `if(ctx->user.exif) goto discard`, `if(ctx->user.text) goto discard`, `if(ctx->user.splt) goto discard`, and `if(!ctx->user.time) memcpy(...)`; H0 leaves every corresponding ctx->user bit unset.
check_exif() validates pointer, length, and byte-order signatures for user-facing struct spng_exif semantics, while H0 supplies eXIf only indirectly as serialized PNG bytes.
recommended_action: Add a structured API-protocol fuzz target that derives spng_offs, spng_exif, text, sPLT, and time metadata from fuzz bytes, invokes the corresponding public metadata setters both before input (encode-only) and before parsing conflicting file chunks, then exercises getters/decoding and context cleanup; include invalid lengths, nullability, signatures, duplicate types, and setter/file precedence.
